summary: Persistent Goal pause/resume with a unified startup gate, schema v13, and dogfood test isolation. records.py adds GoalStatus.paused + GoalPausedError; state.py migrates the goals status CHECK to admit 'paused' (parent-table rebuild with foreign keys deferred inside the copy-then-replace migration; identity/history/usage preserved verbatim, nothing backfilled, failure leaves the original usable) plus gate/CAS store helpers (goal_unfinished, goal_status_for_revision, goal_transition, goal_complete_if_active, attempts_open_for_task). machine.py owns the goal transition table with idempotent pause/resume, gates machine.claim inside its transaction, and makes refresh_run's completion a row-decided active->done CAS so a paused goal is never lifted implicitly and converges at resume. dispatch.py gates planner/replan routing, plan activation, worker dispatch (host/external park and CLI launch), parked-assignment claim, verifier dispatch (host and CLI), and the downgrade reroute — each gate re-read inside the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction that writes the executor placeholder, prompt files written outside the transaction; goal_pause/goal_resume return in-flight ownership (run, revision, assignment, attempts, nonces) with recovery guidance and resume starts nothing; create_goal refuses while a paused (unfinished) goal exists. cli.py adds `orx goal pause|resume` with text and JSON interfaces and explicit idempotent results (changed:false, exit 0). Consumers migrated in sync: schema-version assertions to 13 across the suite, observability schema_gate whitelist 8..13 with the v13 contract amendment (disclosed one-line consumer migration in tests/test_package_acceptance.py, a mechanical schema literal the scope list omitted). The dogfood test now writes its report only to pytest tmp_path and replays usage against a private snapshot copy of the database, with a subprocess regression proving docs/m1.2-report.md and .orx/state.db (+wal/+shm) stay byte-identical while artifacts land under the temporary tree. Race safety proven with independent connections and deterministic barriers: pause vs startup placeholder (both orderings), concurrent claims (single winner), repeated concurrent resumes (flip once), plus real cross-process pause/resume and new-process identity preservation. Full suite: 1092 passed.
